leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members prefer B011, targeted protein degradation, as a single-part prize. They share the view that a bifunctional molecule recruiting an E3 ligase turns binding into elimination and reaches targets that occupancy-based inhibitors cannot, and all four name no approved degrader drug and crowded credit as the main reservations. They differ on laureates: Aili, Aqvist and Linke propose Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, while Chabes proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa and words the citation to cover molecular glues as well as PROTACs. The other four members each prefer a different single-part prize, so a five-member majority for B011 is not yet explicit in the round-1 files.

Brzezinski prefers Gray and Winkler on long-range electron transfer through proteins as a mature, physically stated mechanism confirmed over four decades. This position rests on maturity and mechanistic clarity rather than breadth of opening support, and he himself flags priority overlap with Marcus, Dutton and Moser, Beratan and Onuchic, and Hopfield, plus his own field's proximity.

Somfai prefers Buchwald and Hartwig on Pd-catalysed C-N coupling for daily use in synthesis, thirty years of confirmation, and a clean two-person attribution. He acknowledges the 2010 cross-coupling prize, the possible Kosugi antecedent, and the thinnest opening support on the shortlist.

Sparr prefers Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen on phase separation as a unifying physical-chemical organising principle of the cell. She concedes that in-cell evidence is partly indirect, physiological relevance is debated, and Pappu and Mittag are left unresolved; she lists B011 and B061 as alternatives if the committee finds the biology premature.

Zou prefers Grätzel and O'Regan on dye-sensitised nanocrystalline solar cells as a clear structure-determines-function principle, confirmed for over thirty years and arguably overdue. Practical impact has been overtaken by perovskite cells, and it is open whether Hagfeldt must be added as a third name.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members submitted a single-part prize; no member proposes a shared prize across two ballot items.

B011 is the only ballot item preferred by more than one member (four), and the other four members each list it as an alternative, so all eight files place it in a preferred configuration or alternatives list.

Members who prefer B011 and those who prefer other items agree that its scientific principle (recruiting an E3 ligase to remove a chosen protein) is sound and reproduced by many groups; the open points are maturity and credit, not mechanism.
Every member stated no specific conflict for the shortlisted candidates beyond subject proximity (Brzezinski for B058, Sparr for B035 and B061, Linke for B017, Somfai for synthetic methodology).
scientific_disputes: Whether a prize on B011 should be framed around bifunctional PROTACs only or should also cover the molecular-glue and cereblon mechanism (Chabes includes Handa; Aili, Aqvist and Linke do not).
Whether B058 is a distinct discovery claim or an experimental confirmation of principles anticipated by Marcus (1992), Hopfield, and Dutton and Moser.
Whether C-N coupling (B055) is a new principle or an extension of the field recognised in 2010.
Whether in-cell evidence for liquid-liquid phase separation (B035) is strong enough to treat it as an established principle; Aili and Aqvist rank it low on this ground and Sparr concedes the point.
Whether the dye-sensitised cell (B005) should be weighed by its scientific influence or by its limited commercial reach after perovskites.
attribution_disputes: B011: Ciulli (Aili, Aqvist, Linke) versus Handa (Chabes) as the third laureate beside Crews and Deshaies; Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper, and Ito and Gray from the glue strand, are omitted under any trio.
B035: Pappu and Mittag are central to the physical theory and sequence grammar and are left out of Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.
B055: whether Kosugi's tin-amide precedent should be credited alongside Buchwald and Hartwig.
B005: whether Hagfeldt should be added to Grätzel and O'Regan, which would make three names.
B058: Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic were not nominated alongside Gray and Winkler, so a citation must be narrowly drawn.
maturity_disputes: B011: no degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, and members including Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Linke say the prize could look slightly early; none has verified current trial outcomes.
B035: physiological relevance and artefact concerns (overexpression, indirect in-cell evidence) lead some members to call recognition premature.
B058, B055 and B005 are described by their proponents as mature or overdue, so the contrast with B011 is between validated-but-older work and new work with consequences still emerging.
B008 (nitrogenase) appears as an alternative for Brzezinski, Chabes and Zou, with the structure mature but the catalytic mechanism (N2 binding, E4 state) still debated.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member declared a recusal-level conflict for any shortlisted candidate.
Brzezinski notes scientific proximity to B058 (proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes) and is a Stockholm University colleague of Zou, who is not a candidate.
Sparr notes subject proximity to B035 and B061 (lipid self-assembly and amyloid) and shares Lund University with Linke and Somfai.
Linke notes that B017 (nanopores) is near his own field of nanofabricated devices and that he shares a Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr.
Somfai notes a perspective bias towards synthetic methodology (B055); Aqvist notes a possible bias towards simulation work (B053).
questions_for_round2: Should the B011 citation cover PROTACs only, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, or also the molecular-glue and cereblon strand, which would put Handa in the trio and omit Ciulli, and can the committee defend leaving out Sakamoto, Kim, Ito and Gray in either case?

Do the four B011 supporters hold their first place if no approved degrader exists by the announcement, and what evidence of clinical or practical validation would the other four members need to move to B011?

Can Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr and Zou each state whether they would move to B011 as a single-part prize if their own first choice cannot reach five votes, and which alternative they would choose next?
For B058, what specific discovery distinguishes Gray and Winkler from Marcus, Hopfield, and Dutton and Moser, and can a citation be drawn narrowly enough to stand?
For B035, does the committee consider the in-cell evidence for phase separation sufficient now, and how would credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag be set within three names?
For B055, how should Kosugi's precedent be weighed, and is C-N coupling distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize?
For B005, is Hagfeldt a founding contributor or a later one, and does the later dominance of perovskite cells change the weight of practical impact?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one plurality position, B011 with four explicit supporters and a disagreement over the third laureate, and four members each holding a different single-part first choice, so no ballot item has an explicit five-member majority. The disagreements are mostly about maturity and credit rather than whether the underlying science is correct. Round 2 should decide the B011 laureate set and whether the members with other first choices will move.
